title: canary: add automated feedback loop and granular alerting for performance canaries
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: our canary jobs surface regressions but require manual triage and intervention to adjust exposure. This PR adds an automated feedback loop that tightens or relaxes traffic exposure to new model revisions based on recent canary windows and deterministic thresholds, plus a set of more granular alerting rules to reduce noise during transient ups/downs.

What this changes: 1) canary/feedback: new long‑running worker that consumes canary metrics, computes stability windows, and adjusts per-route exposure percent via the rollout API; 2) metrics: Prometheus rules and alertmanager templates for tiered alerts (warning -> critical) and flapping suppression policy; 3) console: small UX surface showing current exposure and last evaluation decisions; 4) tests: unit tests for decision logic and an integration test that simulates exposure ramps.

Checklist: [x] core decision algorithm implemented and unit tested; [x] Prometheus rules added and linted; [x] API call to rollout controller implemented with idempotency; [x] integration test (canary_ramp_test) added; [ ] docs: follow-up doc for SRE runbook (ENG-2199).

Notes: The decision algorithm is conservative by default (requires 3 sequential stable windows within 10 minutes each to increase exposure) to avoid cascading rollouts. It is parameterized per-environment and per-route. There is a kill switch env var (CANARY_FEEDBACK_ENABLED=false) to restore prior behavior. Links: Linear ENG-2147 for design, internal runbook draft: /docs/runbooks/canary-feedback.md.
commits_summary: 5 commits: add feedback worker and decision engine; add Prometheus alert rules and silencing configuration; add console endpoint and minimal UI; integration test and CI job; cleanup and docs pointer.
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Left a few questions on decision.py around edge cases when a canary becomes noisy mid-window — suggested adding a debounce counter — addressed with a small refactor and unit test.

Priya Nair: Can we make the stability window configurable via API? Concerned about ops needing faster overrides. Author reply: added per-route override via rollout annotations and helm values for defaults.
Samir O'Connor: e2e flaked in CI (timing). Requested stronger test harness. Author reply: added deterministic clock in test and retried CI.
QA (automated): Integration test failed on first run due to race; fixed by improving readiness checks in canary-deployment manifest.
Security review (automated): no new network egress; noted that the worker calls internal rollout API and reuses existing mTLS credentials.
ci_checks: integration-canary: pass (flaky on first run, rerun)
release_notes: Introduce an automated canary feedback loop that adjusts per-route exposure based on recent canary stability windows; adds tiered alerts and flapping suppression. Ops should read the new runbook before enabling in production.
